target_customer: B2B SaaS companies, from early stage startups to larger firms, wanting account-level product analytics
problem: Mixpanel and Amplitude style tools are hard to implement, hard to use and costly, and track users rather than the business accounts a B2B SaaS cares about.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for product analytics, built on Segment data at launch

founders.name: Enzo Avigo
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as product focused; the Launch HN and TechCrunch say both founders left Intercom.

founders.name: Ferruccio Balestreri
previous_startups: Built the technology for altacucina.co, a community for Italian food lovers (per YC page)

investors: Business angels incl. Scott Belsky and Jo of Maze (per Point Nine)

exit.reason: Team joined Amplitude and the standalone product was retired; the company said it was profitable with more than 1,000 startups onboarded and chose Amplitude over moving upmarket or cutting costs for small customers.

competitors.name: Amplitude
competitors.what: Product analytics platform, named by Point Nine as a large incumbent

competitors.name: Mixpanel
competitors.what: Product analytics platform, named by Point Nine as a large incumbent

technical_complexity.rationale: Auto generated metric templates over Segment event data and CRM links is standard data engineering for a six person team; the differentiator was design and defaults, not hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Built on top of Segment and similar to features incumbents could ship; Point Nine framed the edge as design led. Historical dashboards created some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amplitude absorbed the team in 2025 and retired the standalone product.

market_need_then: Point Nine said analytics tools were hard to implement, hard to use and costly (June 2021); the TechCrunch launch piece (2021-05-31) positioned June as making analytics accessible.

branding.name_origin: From the first month of summer, per CEO Enzo Avigo in a 2023 post about the new logo.

identity.logo: New logo and site launched February 2023, designed with eFounders Startup Studio
identity.visual_style: Cornflower blue (#6868F7) and white per Brandfetch; design led, warm
identity.voice_and_tone: Simple, warm and approachable, as a deliberate contrast with cold, intimidating analytics tools

branding.brand_signature: A warm, design led alternative to cold analytics tools

rebrands.why: To feel warmer and more approachable than typical analytics tools

branding.community_and_virality: Frequent Product Hunt launches and a Launch HN thread; no merch or fan communities found.

brand_strength.rationale: Intentional warm positioning and repeated Product Hunt launches helped a small team reach over 1,000 startups, but the brand was never mainstream and the generic name collided with many other Junes.

pivots.why: Launch HN says the founders pivoted to B2B SaaS; exact date not given by the sources I opened

outcome_analysis: June raised about $1.85M in 2021, reached profitability and more than 1,000 startup customers with a small team, but faced Amplitude and Mixpanel and a ceiling on small customers. The founders chose to join Amplitude in 2025 and wound down the product, an acquihire soft landing rather than a failure of cash, helped by capital efficiency and a design led, self serve product.
notes: YC directory marks June Inactive, which is consistent with the 2025 acquihire and product wind down, so exit.type is acquisition. Exit date conflict: the june.so announcement page I fetched is dated August 8, 2025, while a search summary says the announcement was July 8, 2025 with the product ending August 8, 2025. Recorded as 2025-08. Aggregators give totals from about $1.98M to $2M and one lists a $2M pre-seed (trysignalbase); these are unverified and may be the same seed. Amplitude deal price not disclosed. Point Nine named angels as Scott Bellsky (as spelled) of Behance and Jo of Maze; recorded as spelled by the source summary. Launch HN thread is dated 2023 by a search summary, so it is not used as a competitor source. YC lists primary partner Gustaf Alstromer.
